summary: Block notified employees of a separate November round of job cuts affecting Customer Operations, Risk Operations, and Learning & Content Operations, with Cash App and Square staff reported affected. The number of departures is undisclosed. The notice cited better tools for routine tasks but did not explicitly name AI; an earlier SEC filing describes a broader efficiency strategy including AI automation, prioritisation, performance management and team centralisation. This is not evidence that AI directly replaced every affected worker, and February's more than 4,000 cuts are not counted again.
evidenceQuote: We plan to continue to operate at this smaller size and are continuing to look at ways to improve our efficiency through a combination of AI automation, prioritization of our scope, performance management, and centralization of teams and functions to reduce duplication.
notes: Business Insider published its report on November 5, 2026 and reviewed an employee email sent Wednesday, November 4. The email described reducing roles, changing responsibilities and reporting lines; some employees would leave while others would enter consultation. Two people familiar with the matter identified Cash App cuts, while Square employees reported departures on social media. Block declined comment and no total was available. The email referred to using better tools to handle routine tasks and refocusing teams on complex cases and decisions, without explicitly mentioning AI. Block's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q, Management's Discussion and Analysis, page 41, says its February Workforce Plan concluded in Q2 and that separate Q3 efficiency efforts generated immaterial severance costs. Those Q3 costs predate the November notices and are not evidence of the size or precise cause of this November round. The filing provides company-stated strategic context, not a direct attribution of all new cuts to AI. The existing February event remains unchanged; this entry adds no jobs to the aggregate until a reliable count is disclosed. Geography denotes company-level coverage; no country distribution was established.

sources.name: Business Insider (employee notice and reporting on the second round)
